state_background_check.value: No — Illinois's constitutional felony bar applies only to "an office created by this Constitution" (Illinois state and local offices) by its own text, not federal office; separately, the U.S. Constitution's own qualifications for Congress (age, citizenship, residency) can't be added to by any state, so this doesn't reach U.S. House or Senate candidates either way
state_background_check.snippet: Ill. Const. art. XIII, § 1: "A person convicted of a felony, bribery, perjury or other infamous crime shall be ineligible to hold an office created by this Constitution. Eligibility may be restored as provided by law." Congressional qualifications are set exclusively by the U.S. Constitution, confirmed per https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/R41946.html: "the Framers intended the Constitution to be the exclusive source of qualifications for Members of Congress, and that the Framers thereby 'divested' States of any power to add qualifications."

platform.value: Active championing of voting rights with support for initiatives like the For the People Act and the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act to enhance voter access, counteract suppression, and ensure fair representation
platform.snippet: Active championing of voting rights aligns with a historic push for electoral fairness, exemplified by key legislative milestones such as the Voting Rights Act of 1965, which sought to eliminate racial discrimination in voting, and more recent efforts like the For the People Act and the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act. Support for these initiatives aims to enhance voter access, counteract suppression, and ensure fair representation.

platform.snippet: Strong advocacy for Medicare for All reflects a broader push for universal health coverage and addressing disparities in the U.S. healthcare system.

platform.value: Supports legislation aimed at ensuring comprehensive healthcare access for women's health and reproductive rights, including endorsement of the Women's Health Protection Act to safeguard reproductive freedoms
platform.snippet: A strong advocate for women s health and reproductive rights, Congressman Jonathan Jackson supports legislation aimed at ensuring comprehensive healthcare access. This advocacy builds on key historical milestones, such as the 1973 Roe v. Wade decision and the Women s Health Protection Act, which he endorses to safeguard reproductive freedoms.

platform.value: Advocates for equal and adequate education, including expanding funding for under-resourced schools and improving early childhood education
platform.snippet: Congressman Jonathan Jackson advocates for equal and adequate education, drawing from his experience as a professor at Chicago State University. His efforts align with key legislation like the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 and its reauthorization, the Every Student Succeeds Act of 2015. These laws aimed to close achievement gaps and increase support for disadvantaged schools. Jackson’s push includes expanding funding for under-resourced schools and improving early childhood education.
